data.narrative:
Elementl Power is a Series A nuclear energy company that has raised $50M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 11 entities across the nuclear sector—3 public firms (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private companies including Fuse Energy, Helion, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, and Oklo—at stages ranging from Seed through Series B.

Two triangulation methods apply here. Stage-progression analysis uses the $50M raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage progression, yielding $100M. Peer-median analysis spans 3 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comps: Valar Atomics at $6.0B (Series B), Nano Nuclear Energy at $808M (Seed), and Fuse Energy at $200M (Series A). The median valuation across these three is $808M, with a range of $200M to $6.0B.

The two methods triangulate to a valuation range of $85M (low) to $929M (high), with a median of $454M. The wide spread reflects material stage and capital-intensity variance within the peer set. Key uncertainties include technology maturity relative to comps, path to commercialization, and the high volatility characteristic of early-stage nuclear ventures. Stage-progression suggests more conservative positioning near $85M–$100M, while peer benchmarking supports the higher range contingent on comparable technical and market progress.
